nodes.content: Design a distributed scheduler for preemptible gang jobs that reconciles tenant fairness, placement constraints, and recovery from scheduler partitions.
requirements: Prevent conflicting resource assignments during partitions, including stale schedulers and partially completed gang reservations.
After connectivity stabilizes, restore scheduling progress within 30 seconds while preventing starvation under feasible demand.

nodes.content: Use quorum-fenced scheduler epochs, worker-verified atomic gang commits, tenant-weighted aging with constraint-aware preemption, and five-second failover leases.
How do workers identify and release partial gang reservations when a scheduler loses its lease mid-commit?
Epoch-fenced workers expiring uncommitted gang-ID reservations after five seconds will clear orphaned holds within ten seconds without conflicting assignments.
Run GangFault-1k mid-commit partition tests; verify stale-epoch rejection, orphan-hold clearance within ten seconds, and zero duplicate allocations.
Execute GangFault-1k with 1,000 mid-commit partitions; record stale-epoch rejections, orphan-hold clearance latency, and duplicate allocations.
GangFault-1k: maximum orphan-hold clearance was 8.2 seconds; all stale epochs were rejected, with zero duplicate allocations.
Adopt epoch-fenced five-second reservation expiry: GangFault-1k cleared orphan holds within 8.2 seconds without duplicate allocations.
GangFault-1k report records 1,000 partition traces, 8.2-second maximum orphan clearance, complete stale-epoch rejection, and zero duplicate allocations.
Replay GangFault-1k report’s worst mid-commit traces with 64-worker placement constraints; measure stale-epoch rejection, orphan clearance, and duplicate allocations.
In 64-worker constrained replays, delayed commit propagation caused two duplicate allocations when prepared workers expired already-committed gang slots.
Do epoch-fenced atomic commits remain conflict-free when constrained placements delay commit propagation beyond five-second reservation expiry?
Quorum-log gang commits before worker activation; retain uncertain slots until reconciliation, then resume weighted-deficit, constraint-aware preemption within 30 seconds.
Implement quorum-logged gang commits, worker reconciliation, weighted-deficit preemption; test 64-worker partitions for zero conflicts, ≤30-second recovery, and feasible-tenant starvation.
Replay GangFault-1k report traces against quorum-logged commits and worker reconciliation; measure duplicate allocations and recovery latency on 64 workers.
GangFault-1k replay bundle contains 64-worker partition traces, quorum-commit reconciliation logs, duplicate-allocation counts, and recovery-latency measurements.
Audit GangFault-1k bundle; rerun partitions under p1 and p2 with contention, comparing duplicate allocations, recovery, and tenant wait.
64-worker replays: p2 had zero duplicates versus p1’s two; p2 recovered within 24 seconds, with longest feasible-tenant wait 82 seconds.
Can p2 keep feasible-tenant wait below 120 seconds under sustained contention and restrictive gang placements?
Under sustained contention, weighted-deficit aging and constraint-aware preemption keep maximum feasible-tenant wait below 120 seconds across 64 workers.
Compare p1/p2 in 30-minute, 64-worker constrained-gang partition tests with eight-second commit delays; measure duplicates and maximum feasible-tenant wait.
In 30-minute constrained tests, p2’s maximum feasible-tenant wait was 109 seconds, with zero duplicates despite eight-second commit delays.
Replace p1’s expiry-only commits with p2’s quorum-logged reconciliation: zero duplicates, 24-second recovery, and 109-second maximum feasible-tenant wait.
Use Raft-elected single-writer scheduling, worker-acknowledged fencing, durable gang bindings, and aging-based fairness with 20-second failover.
Can worker-acknowledged fencing complete within 20 seconds when partitioned workers hold durable gang bindings?
After connectivity stabilizes, worker-acknowledged epoch fencing completes within 20 seconds across 64 workers without releasing committed gang bindings.
Replay GangFault-1k bundle across 64 workers; time post-reconnection fencing acknowledgments and audit committed gang bindings for unintended release.
GangFault-1k replay: fencing acknowledgments took up to 26.4 seconds after reconnection across 64 workers; no committed bindings were released.
Replay GangFault-1k with 10% delayed worker reconnects; measure fencing acknowledgment latency and committed-binding retention against the 20-second target.
With 10% delayed reconnects, all workers acknowledged fencing within 18.7 seconds after full reconnection; no committed bindings were released.
Do not rely on p3’s 20-second fencing target: one replay took 26.4 seconds despite another completing in 18.7 seconds.
Quorum-issued per-resource tokens and logged gang decisions gate activation; placement-aware deficit preemption resumes on reconciled workers without global fencing.
Implement token validation and logged gang decisions; replay partitions to measure duplicate allocations, recovery within 30 seconds, and feasible-tenant wait.
Replay GangFault-1k bundle on 64 workers with quorum tokens and logged gang decisions; measure duplicates, recovery, and feasible-tenant wait.
TokenGang-64 replay report contains quorum-token validation traces, logged gang decisions, duplicate-allocation counts, recovery latencies, and feasible-tenant waits.
Audit TokenGang-64 traces and rerun partial-commit partitions; check duplicate allocations, 30-second recovery, and 120-second feasible-tenant wait.
TokenGang-64 partial-commit replays produced zero duplicate allocations, 21-second maximum recovery, and 97-second maximum feasible-tenant wait.
Adopt p4’s quorum tokens and logged gang decisions: TokenGang-64 showed zero duplicates, 21-second recovery, and 97-second feasible-tenant wait.
Quorum-lease rack shards; durably commit gangs before activation, reconcile holds within 25 seconds after reconnection, and age placement-aware tenant deficits.
Can cross-rack gangs acquire shard leases atomically without stranded holds delaying reconciliation beyond 25 seconds?
A quorum-logged gang coordinator releases incomplete cross-rack shard holds within 25 seconds without activating partial gangs.
Instrument cross-rack lease acquisition and coordinator decisions; inject mid-reservation partitions, then measure hold release and partial activation.
Extend TokenGang-64 traces across four racks; inject coordinator partitions mid-reservation and measure hold-release latency, partial activations, and recovery.
Four-rack replays released incomplete holds within 22 seconds with zero partial activations, but shard-lease contention delayed scheduling recovery 37 seconds.
Stress TokenGang-64 with concurrent cross-rack lease requests and coordinator failover; check atomic activation and 25-second incomplete-hold release.
Under concurrent cross-rack requests and coordinator failover, incomplete holds persisted 31 seconds; no partial gangs activated.
Reject p5’s rack-shard leases: contention yielded 37-second recovery, and failover stranded incomplete holds for 31 seconds.
Prioritized quorum aborts and per-resource tokens clear holds within 25 seconds, prevent partial activation, and restore scheduling within 30 seconds.
Replay four-rack failovers with prioritized aborts and per-resource tokens; verify hold release within 25 seconds and recovery within 30 seconds.
Gate TokenGang-64’s prioritized-abort implementation on n41’s rack-lease rejection; replay four-rack failovers against p5, measuring hold release, partial activations, recovery.
Four-rack failovers: prioritized aborts cleared holds in 19 seconds; recovery took 26 seconds versus p5’s 37, without partial activations.
Retain p4 tokens with prioritized quorum aborts, not p5 rack leases: 19-second hold clearance and 26-second recovery.
